1416:                 ]
1417:             )
1418:             for sid
1419:             in dataset["sample_id"]
1420:         ],
1421:         dtype=np.int64,
1422:     )
1423: 
1424:     if X_raw.shape != (
1425:         179,
1426:         14,
1427:     ):
1428: 
1429:         raise RuntimeError(
1430:             f"Expected X shape (179, 14), got {X_raw.shape}."
1431:         )
1432: 
1433:     if y.shape != (179,):
1434: 
1435:         raise RuntimeError(
1436:             f"Expected y shape (179,), got {y.shape}."
1437:         )
1438: 
1439:     if not np.all(
1440:         np.isfinite(X_raw)
1441:     ):
1442: 
1443:         raise RuntimeError(
1444:             "Historical expression matrix contains "
1445:             "non-finite values."
1446:         )
1447: 
1448:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1449:     # 6. Run exact forward pass.
1450:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1451: 
1452:     (
1453:         X_normalized,
1454:         hidden_pre,
1455:         hidden,
1456:         output,
1457:     ) = forward_pass(
1458:         X_raw
1459:     )
1460: 
1461:     cancer_activation = (
1462:         output[:, 0]
1463:     )
1464: 
1465:     control_activation = (
1466:         output[:, 1]
1467:     )
1468: 
1469:     predicted_class = (
1470:         cancer_activation
1471:         > control_activation
1472:     ).astype(int)
1473: 
1474:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1475:     # 7. Metrics.
1476:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1477: 
1478:     # Avoid requiring sklearn for the core reproduction.
1479:     try:
1480: 
1481:         from sklearn.metrics import (
1482:             accuracy_score,
1483:             confusion_matrix,
1484:             roc_auc_score,
1485:             sensitivity_score,
1486:             specificity_score,
1487:         )
1488: 
1489:     except ImportError:
1490: 
1491:         accuracy_score = None
1492:         confusion_matrix = None
1493:         roc_auc_score = None
1494:         sensitivity_score = None
1495:         specificity_score = None
1496: 
1497:     if roc_auc_score is not None:
1498: 
1499:         auc = float(
1500:             roc_auc_score(
1501:                 y,
1502:                 cancer_activation,
1503:             )
1504:         )
1505: 
1506:         accuracy = float(
1507:             accuracy_score(
1508:                 y,
1509:                 predicted_class,
1510:             )
1511:         )
1512: 
1513:         cm = confusion_matrix(
1514:             y,
1515:             predicted_class,
1516:         )
1517: 
1518:         tn, fp, fn, tp = (
1519:             int(cm[0, 0]),
1520:             int(cm[0, 1]),
1521:             int(cm[1, 0]),
1522:             int(cm[1, 1]),
1523:         )
1524: 
1525:     else:
1526: 
1527:         auc = None
1528: 
1529:         tn = int(
1530:             np.sum(
1531:                 (y == 0)
1532:                 & (predicted_class == 0)
1533:             )
1534:         )
1535: 
1536:         fp = int(
1537:             np.sum(
1538:                 (y == 0)
1539:                 & (predicted_class == 1)
1540:             )
1541:         )
1542: 
1543:         fn = int(
1544:             np.sum(
1545:                 (y == 1)
1546:                 & (predicted_class == 0)
1547:             )
1548:         )
1549: 
1550:         tp = int(
1551:             np.sum(
1552:                 (y == 1)
1553:                 & (predicted_class == 1)
1554:             )
1555:         )
1556: 
1557:         accuracy = (
1558:             (tp + tn)
1559:             / len(y)
1560:         )
1561: 
1562:     sensitivity = (
1563:         tp / (tp + fn)
1564:         if (tp + fn) > 0
1565:         else float("nan")
1566:     )
1567: 
1568:     specificity = (
1569:         tn / (tn + fp)
1570:         if (tn + fp) > 0
1571:         else float("nan")
1572:     )
1573: 
1574:     ties = int(
1575:         np.sum(
1576:             np.isclose(
1577:                 cancer_activation,
1578:                 control_activation,
1579:                 rtol=0.0,
1580:                 atol=1e-12,
1581:             )
1582:         )
1583:     )
1584: 
1585:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1586:     # 8. Prediction table.
1587:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1588: 
1589:     predictions = dataset[
1590:         ["sample_id"]
1591:     ].copy()
1592: 
1593:     predictions["diagnosis"] = [
1594:         metadata.loc[
1595:             sid,
1596:             "diagnosis",
1597:         ]
1598:         for sid in predictions[
1599:             "sample_id"
1600:         ]
1601:     ]
1602: 
1603:     predictions["true_label"] = y
1604: 
1605:     predictions[
1606:         "cancer_activation"
1607:     ] = cancer_activation
1608: 
1609:     predictions[
1610:         "controls_or_borderline_activation"
1611:     ] = control_activation
1612: 
1613:     predictions[
1614:         "predicted_label"
1615:     ] = predicted_class
1616: 
1617:     predictions[
1618:         "predicted_class"
1619:     ] = np.where(
1620:         predicted_class == 1,
1621:         "Ovarian Cancer",
1622:         "Controls or Borderline",
1623:     )
1624: 
1625:     predictions.to_csv(
1626:         PREDICTIONS_OUTPUT,
1627:         index=False,
1628:     )
1629: 
1630:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1631:     # 9. Forward-pass trace.
1632:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1633: 
1634:     trace = dataset[
1635:         ["sample_id"]
1636:         + FEATURES
1637:     ].copy()
1638: 
1639:     for i in range(14):
1640: 
1641:         trace[
1642:             f"normalized_{i+1:02d}"
1643:         ] = X_normalized[:, i]
1644: 
1645:     for i in range(7):
1646: 
1647:         trace[
1648:             f"hidden_{i+14}"
1649:         ] = hidden[:, i]
1650: 
1651:     trace[
1652:         "output_21_cancer"
1653:     ] = output[:, 0]
1654: 
1655:     trace[
1656:         "output_22_controls_or_borderline"
1657:     ] = output[:, 1]
1658: 
1659:     trace.to_csv(
1660:         TRACE_OUTPUT,
1661:         index=False,
1662:     )
1663: 
1664:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1665:     # 10. Mapping.
1666:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1667: 
1668:     save_mapping(
1669:         dataset,
1670:         metadata,
1671:     )
1672: 
1673:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1674:     # 11. Results.
1675:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1676: 
1677:     results = {
1678:         "dataset": {
1679:             "source": "eLife Supplemental Dataset 2",
1680:             "representation": (
1681:                 "batch adjusted, log10-transformed "
1682:                 "miRNA expression"
1683:             ),
1684:             "patients": int(len(y)),
1685:             "features": 14,
1686:             "feature_names": FEATURES,
1687:         },
1688: 
1689:         "sample_order": {
1690:             "cohort2_count": 120,
1691:             "cohort1_count_after_e1056_exclusion": 59,
1692:             "total": 179,
1693:             "excluded_sample": "e1056",
1694:         },
1695: 
1696:         "labels": {
1697:             "cancer": int(np.sum(y == 1)),
1698:             "non_cancer": int(np.sum(y == 0)),
1699:         },
1700: 
1701:         "model": {
1702:             "architecture": "14-7-2",
1703:             "hidden_activation": "tanh",
1704:             "output_activation": "tanh",
1705:             "output_neuron_21": "Ovarian Cancer",
1706:             "output_neuron_22": (
1707:                 "Controls or Borderline"
1708:             ),
1709:             "probability_transformation_used": False,
1710:         },
1711: 
1712:         "normalization": {
1713:             "formula": (
1714:                 "normalized = raw * scale + shift"
1715:             ),
1716:             "verified_against_pmml_endpoints": True,
1717:         },
1718: 
1719:         "metrics_on_historical_179_patients": {
1720:             "auc": auc,
1721:             "accuracy": accuracy,
1722:             "sensitivity": sensitivity,
1723:             "specificity": specificity,
1724:             "tp": tp,
1725:             "tn": tn,

1729:         },
1730: 
1731:         "files": {
1732:             "predictions": str(
1733:                 PREDICTIONS_OUTPUT
1734:             ),
1735:             "forward_trace": str(
1736:                 TRACE_OUTPUT
1737:             ),
1738:             "sample_mapping": str(
1739:                 MAPPING_OUTPUT
1740:             ),
1741:         },
1742:

1745: 
1746:     RESULTS_OUTPUT.write_text(
1747:         json.dumps(
1748:             results,

### scripts\reproduce_original_historical_standalone.py
1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: 
3: """
4: STANDALONE HISTORICAL REPRODUCTION OF THE ORIGINAL eLIFE
5: GSE94533 14-miRNA NEURAL NETWORK
6: 
7: This script intentionally does NOT use the previous
8: reproduce_original_pmml_historical_data.py script.
9: 
10: Reason:
11:     that script accumulated several incorrect assumptions about
12:     Supplemental Dataset 2 sample identifiers.
13: 
14: This standalone implementation directly establishes:
15: 
16:     Supplemental Dataset 2
17:             |
18:             v
19:     historical 179 sample columns
20:             |
21:             v
22:     first 120 positional columns -> Cohort 2 IDs
23:     final 59 explicit columns    -> explicit Cohort 1 IDs
24:             |
25:             v
26:     exact 14 PMML miRNAs
27:             |
28:             v
29:     PMML normalization
30:             |
31:             v
32:     14 -> 7 tanh -> 2 tanh
33:             |
34:             v
35:     cancer vs non-cancer prediction
36: 
37: NO MODEL TRAINING IS PERFORMED.
38: 
39: IMPORTANT:
40: ------------
41: We deliberately preserve the historical supplementary dataset as it
42: is represented in Supplemental Dataset 2.
43: 
44: We do NOT remove E-1056 merely because an earlier cleaned dataset
45: removed it.
46: 
47: The historical representation must be reproduced independently from
48: our later cleaned modern dataset.
49: """

146: # =====================================================================
147: # SAMPLE ID NORMALIZATION
148: # =====================================================================
149: 
150: def normalize_id(value: object) -> str:
151: 
152:     if value is None:
153:         return ""
154: 
155:     if pd.isna(value):
156:         return ""
157: 
158:     s = str(value).strip().lower()
159: 
160:     # Excel numeric representation:
161:     # 50217.0 -> 50217
162:     if re.fullmatch(r"\d+\.0+", s):
163:         s = s.split(".", 1)[0]
164: 
165:     # E-1001 -> e1001
166:     s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", s)
167: 
168:     return s
169: 
170: 
171: # =====================================================================
172: # READ ORIGINAL PROCESSED WORKBOOK SAMPLE ORDER
173: # =====================================================================
174: 
175: def get_processed_sample_order():
176: 
177:     print()
178:     print("=" * 100)
179:     print("RECOVERING ORIGINAL PROCESSED-WORKBOOK SAMPLE ORDER")
180:     print("=" * 100)
181: 
182:     def read_order(path):
183: 
184:         header = pd.read_excel(
185:             path,
186:             sheet_name="mirna_tpm",
187:             header=2,
188:             nrows=0,
189:             engine="openpyxl",
190:         )
191: 
192:         result = []
193: 
194:         for column in header.columns:
195: 
196:             normalized = normalize_id(column)
197: 
198:             if not normalized:
199:                 continue
200: 
201:             # Exclude metadata columns.
202:             if normalized in {
203:                 "name",
204:                 "sequence",
205:                 "namecount",
206:                 "identicalmirnas",
207:             }:
208:                 continue
209: 
210:             # GSE94533 sample identifiers are either:
211:             #   e#### / E-####
212:             # or numeric identifiers.
213:             if normalized.startswith("e"):
214: 
215:                 if normalized[1:].isdigit():
216:                     result.append(normalized)
217: 
218:             elif normalized.isdigit():
219: 
220:                 result.append(normalized)
221: 
222:         return result
223: 
224:     cohort1 = read_order(COHORT1_XLSX)
225:     cohort2 = read_order(COHORT2_XLSX)
226: 
227:     print()
228:     print(f"Cohort 1 samples: {len(cohort1)}")
229:     print(f"Cohort 2 samples: {len(cohort2)}")
230: 
231:     print()
232:     print("Cohort 2 first 10:")
233:     for x in cohort2[:10]:
234:         print(f"  {x}")
235: 
236:     print()
237:     print("Cohort 1 first 10:")
238:     for x in cohort1[:10]:
239:         print(f"  {x}")
240: 
241:     if len(cohort2) != 120:
242:         raise RuntimeError(
243:             "Expected exactly 120 Cohort 2 samples, "
244:             f"found {len(cohort2)}."
245:         )
246: 
247:     if len(cohort1) != 60:
248:         raise RuntimeError(
249:             "Expected exactly 60 Cohort 1 samples, "
250:             f"found {len(cohort1)}."
251:         )
252: 
253:     return cohort2, cohort1

306:                 total_identifier_like += 1
307:

309:             numeric_count >= 100

311:         ):

314:

343:     )

387: 
388:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
389:     # Recover the actual sample IDs.
390:     #
391:     # Dataset 2 uses:
392:     #
393:     #   first 120 columns:
394:     #       1, 2, ..., 120
395:     #
396:     #   final 59 columns:
397:     #       explicit Cohort 1 identifiers
398:     #
399:     # The first 120 are POSITION NUMBERS.
400:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
401: 
402:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
403:     # ROBUST CHECK FOR DATASET 2 POSITIONAL HEADERS
404:     #
405:     # Excel/pandas may represent:
406:     #
407:     #     1
408:     #     2.0
409:     #     3.0
410:     #     ...
411:     #
412:     # as different Python/numpy types.
413:     #
414:     # Therefore we compare numerically rather than comparing strings.
415:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
416: 
417:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
418:     # Robust Dataset 2 positional-header detection.
419:     #
420:     # The first 120 Dataset 2 columns may be represented by pandas
421:     # as Python ints, floats, or NumPy floating-point values.
422:     #
423:     # Do NOT use sample_ids here because that list is constructed
424:     # later in this function.
425:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
426:     
427:     first_120_are_positions = False
428:     
429:     try:
430:         first_120_raw = [
431:             raw.iloc[header_row, column]
432:             for column in range(1, 121)
433:         ]
434:     
435:         first_120_are_positions = (
436:             len(first_120_raw) == 120
437:             and all(
438:                 float(value) == float(position)
439:                 for position, value
440:                 in enumerate(
441:                     first_120_raw,
442:                     start=1,
443:                 )
444:             )
445:         )
446:     
447:     except (TypeError, ValueError, IndexError):
448:         first_120_are_positions = False
449: 
450:     for i in range(120):
451: 
452:         value = raw_header_ids[i]
453: 
454:         try:
455:             numeric_value = float(value)
456: 
457:         except (TypeError, ValueError):
458:             first_120_are_positions = False
459:             break
460: 
461:         if not math.isfinite(numeric_value):
462:             first_120_are_positions = False
463:             break
464: 
465:         expected_value = float(i + 1)
466: 
467:         if not math.isclose(
468:             numeric_value,
469:             expected_value,
470:             rel_tol=0.0,
471:             abs_tol=1e-9,
472:         ):
473:             first_120_are_positions = False
474:             break
475: 
476:     if not first_120_are_positions:
477: 
478:         raise RuntimeError(
479:             "Dataset 2 does not have the expected first 120 "
480:             "positional headers 1..120."
481:         )
482: 
483:     print()
484:     print(
485:         "CONFIRMED:"
486:     )
487:     print(
488:         "  Dataset 2 columns 1-120 are positional sample numbers."
489:     )
490:     print(
491:         "  Dataset 2 columns 121-179 contain explicit IDs."
492:     )
493: 
494:     cohort2_order, cohort1_order = (
495:         get_processed_sample_order()
496:     )
497: 
498:     historical_sample_ids = (
499:         cohort2_order
500:         + normalized_header_ids[120:]
501:     )
502: 
503:     print()
504:     print(
505:         f"Recovered historical sample count: "
506:         f"{len(historical_sample_ids)}"
507:     )
508: 
509:     if len(historical_sample_ids) != 179:
510: 
511:         raise RuntimeError(
512:             "Historical sample list does not contain 179 samples."
513:         )
514: 
515:     if len(set(historical_sample_ids)) != 179:
516: 
517:         duplicates = []
518: 
519:         seen = set()
520: 
521:         for value in historical_sample_ids:
522: 
523:             if value in seen:
524:                 duplicates.append(value)
525: 
526:             seen.add(value)
527: 
528:         raise RuntimeError(
529:             "Historical sample IDs are not unique.\n"
530:             + "\n".join(
531:                 f"  {x}"
532:                 for x in sorted(set(duplicates))
533:             )
534:         )
535: 
536:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
537:     # IMPORTANT:
538:     #
539:     # We do NOT impose the previous E-1056 exclusion here.
540:     #
541:     # Dataset 2 is the historical representation being reproduced.
542:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
543: 
544:     print()
545:     print(
546:         "Historical E-1056 present:"
547:         f" {'e1056' in historical_sample_ids}"
548:     )
549: 
550:     if "e1056" in historical_sample_ids:
551: 
552:         print()
553:         print(
554:             "NOTE: E-1056 is present in Supplemental Dataset 2."
555:         )
556: 
557:         print(
558:             "Therefore it is being retained for this historical"
559:         )
560: 
561:         print(
562:             "reproduction. We will not apply the later cleaned-dataset"
563:         )
564: 
565:         print(
566:             "exclusion rule here."
567:         )
568: 
569:     print()
570:     print(
571:         "FIRST 10 HISTORICAL SAMPLE MAPPINGS:"
572:     )
573: 
574:     for position in range(10):
575: 
576:         print(
577:             f"  Dataset2 position {position + 1:3d}"
578:             f" -> {historical_sample_ids[position]}"
579:         )
580: 
581:     print()
582:     print(
583:         "LAST 10 HISTORICAL SAMPLE MAPPINGS:"
584:     )
585: 
586:     for position in range(169, 179):
587: 
588:         print(
589:             f"  Dataset2 position {position + 1:3d}"
590:             f" -> {historical_sample_ids[position]}"
591:         )
592: 
593:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
594:     # Locate exact feature rows.
595:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
596: 
597:     feature_rows = {}
598: 
599:     for feature in FEATURES:
600: 
601:         matches = []
602: 
603:         for r in range(
604:             header_row + 1,
605:             len(raw),
606:         ):
607: 
608:             value = raw.iloc[
609:                 r,
610:                 feature_column,
611:             ]
612: 
613:             if (
614:                 not pd.isna(value)
615:                 and str(value).strip() == feature
616:             ):
617:                 matches.append(r)
618: 
619:         if len(matches) != 1:
620: 
621:             raise RuntimeError(
622:                 f"Feature {feature!r} was found "
623:                 f"{len(matches)} times."
624:             )
625: 
626:         feature_rows[feature] = matches[0]
627: 
628:     print()
629:     print(
630:         f"Exact PMML features found: {len(feature_rows)}"
631:     )
632: 
633:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
634:     # Construct matrix.
635:     #
636:     # Rows = patients
637:     # Columns = exact 14 miRNAs.
638:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
639: 
640:     matrix = np.zeros(
641:         (179, 14),
642:         dtype=np.float64,
643:     )
644: 
645:     for j, feature in enumerate(FEATURES):
646: 
647:         row = feature_rows[feature]
648: 
649:         values = []
650: 
651:         for c in sample_columns:
652: 
653:             value = raw.iloc[row, c]
654: 
655:             if pd.isna(value):
656: 
657:                 raise RuntimeError(
658:                     f"Missing Dataset 2 value for "
659:                     f"{feature}, column {c}."
660:                 )
661: 
662:             values.append(float(value))
663: 
664:         matrix[:, j] = values
665: 
666:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
667:     # Create patient-level dataframe.
668:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
669: 
670:     df = pd.DataFrame(
671:         matrix,
672:         columns=FEATURES,
673:     )
674: 
675:     df.insert(
676:         0,
677:         "sample_id",
678:         historical_sample_ids,
679:     )
680: 
681:     print()
682:     print(
683:         "Historical representation:"
684:     )
685:     print(
686:         "  batch adjusted"
687:     )
688:     print(
689:         "  log10 transformed"
690:     )
691:     print(
692:         f"  patients: {len(df)}"
693:     )
694:     print(
695:         f"  PMML features: {len(FEATURES)}"
696:     )
697: 
698:     if not np.isfinite(matrix).all():
699: 
700:         raise RuntimeError(
701:             "Historical matrix contains non-finite values."
702:         )
703: 
704:     return df
705:

711: def load_diagnosis():
712: 
713:     print()
714:     print("=" * 100)
715:     print("LOADING GEO DIAGNOSIS METADATA")
716:     print("=" * 100)
717: 
718:     metadata = pd.read_csv(
719:         GEO_METADATA
720:     )
721: 
722:     metadata["normalized_id"] = (
723:         metadata["title"].map(normalize_id)
724:     )
725: 
726:     metadata = metadata[
727:         metadata["normalized_id"] != ""
728:     ].copy()
729: 
730:     lookup = {}
731: 
732:     for _, row in metadata.iterrows():
733: 
734:         sid = row["normalized_id"]
735: 
736:         if sid in lookup:
737: 
738:             raise RuntimeError(
739:                 "Duplicate GEO sample identifier: "
740:                 f"{sid}"
741:             )
742: 
743:         lookup[sid] = row
744: 
745:     print()
746:     print(
747:         f"GEO diagnosis records: {len(lookup)}"
748:     )
749: 
750:     return lookup

753: # =====================================================================
754: # LOCAL NAME HELPER
755: # =====================================================================
756: 
757: def local_name(element):
758: 
759:     if "}" in element.tag:
760: 
761:         return element.tag.rsplit(
762:             "}",
763:             1,
764:         )[1]
765: 
766:     return element.tag

768: 
769: # =====================================================================
770: # PARSE PMML
771: # =====================================================================
772: 
773: def parse_pmml():
774: 
775:     print()
776:     print("=" * 100)
777:     print("PARSING ORIGINAL PMML")
778:     print("=" * 100)
779: 
780:     root = ET.parse(
781:         PMML_PATH
782:     ).getroot()
783: 
784:     neural_networks = []
785: 
786:     for element in root.iter():
787: 
788:         if local_name(element) == "NeuralNetwork":
789: 
790:             neural_networks.append(element)
791: 
792:     if len(neural_networks) != 1:
793: 
794:         raise RuntimeError(
795:             f"Expected exactly one NeuralNetwork; "
796:             f"found {len(neural_networks)}."
797:         )
798: 
799:     network = neural_networks[0]
800: 
801:     model_name = network.attrib.get(
802:         "modelName"
803:     )
804: 
805:     function_name = network.attrib.get(
806:         "functionName"
807:     )
808: 
809:     print()
810:     print(
811:         f"modelName: {model_name}"
812:     )
813: 
814:     print(
815:         f"functionName: {function_name}"
816:     )
817: 
818:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
819:     # Inputs
820:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
821: 
822:     pmml_inputs = []
823: 
824:     for element in network:
825: 
826:         if local_name(element) != "NeuralInputs":
827:             continue
828: 
829:         for neural_input in element:
830: 
831:             if local_name(neural_input) != "NeuralInput":
832:                 continue
833: 
834:             norm_continuous = None
835: 
836:             for child in neural_input.iter():
837: 
838:                 if local_name(child) == "NormContinuous":
839: 
840:                     norm_continuous = child
841:                     break
842: 
843:             if norm_continuous is None:
844: 
845:                 continue
846: 
847:             field = norm_continuous.attrib[
848:                 "field"
849:             ]
850: 
851:             shift = float(
852:                 norm_continuous.attrib[
853:                     "shift"
854:                 ]
855:             )
856: 
857:             scale = float(
858:                 norm_continuous.attrib[
859:                     "scale"
860:                 ]
861:             )
862: 
863:             linear_norms = []
864: 
865:             for child in norm_continuous:
866: 
867:                 if local_name(child) == "LinearNorm":
868: 
869:                     linear_norms.append(
870:                         (
871:                             float(
872:                                 child.attrib["orig"]
873:                             ),
874:                             float(
875:                                 child.attrib["norm"]
876:                             ),
877:                         )
878:                     )
879: 
880:             pmml_inputs.append(
881:                 {
882:                     "field": field,
883:                     "shift": shift,
884:                     "scale": scale,
885:                     "linear_norms": linear_norms,
886:                 }
887:             )
888: 
889:     if len(pmml_inputs) != 14:
890: 
891:         raise RuntimeError(
892:             "Expected 14 PMML neural inputs; "
893:             f"found {len(pmml_inputs)}."
894:         )
895: 
896:     pmml_feature_names = [
897:         x["field"]
898:         for x in pmml_inputs
899:     ]
900: 
901:     print()
902:     print(
903:         "PMML input features:"
904:     )
905: 
906:     for i, feature in enumerate(
907:         pmml_feature_names,
908:         start=1,
909:     ):
910: 
911:         print(
912:             f"  {i:2d}. {feature}"
913:         )
914: 
915:     if pmml_feature_names != FEATURES:
916: 
917:         raise RuntimeError(
918:             "PMML feature order does not exactly match "
919:             "the recovered 14-feature order.\n"
920:             f"PMML: {pmml_feature_names}\n"
921:             f"Expected: {FEATURES}"
922:         )
923: 
924:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
925:     # Neural layers
926:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
927: 
928:     layers = []
929: 
930:     for element in network:
931: 
932:         if local_name(element) != "NeuralLayer":
933:             continue
934: 
935:         activation = element.attrib.get(
936:             "activation"
937:         )
938: 
939:         neurons = []
940: 
941:         for neuron in element:
942: 
943:             if local_name(neuron) != "Neuron":
944:                 continue
945: 
946:             neuron_id = neuron.attrib.get(
947:                 "id"
948:             )
949: 
950:             bias = float(
951:                 neuron.attrib.get(
952:                     "bias",
953:                     "0",
954:                 )
955:             )
956: 
957:             connections = {}
958: 
959:             for child in neuron:
960: 
961:                 if local_name(child) != "Con":
962:                     continue
963: 
964:                 source = child.attrib.get(
965:                     "from"
966:                 )
967: 
968:                 weight = float(
969:                     child.attrib.get(
970:                         "weight",
971:                         "0",
972:                     )
973:                 )
974: 
975:                 connections[source] = weight
976: 
977:             neurons.append(
978:                 {
979:                     "id": neuron_id,
980:                     "bias": bias,
981:                     "connections": connections,
982:                 }
983:             )
984: 
985:         layers.append(
986:             {
987:                 "activation": activation,
988:                 "neurons": neurons,
989:             }
990:         )
991: 
992:     if len(layers) != 2:
993: 
994:         raise RuntimeError(
995:             f"Expected 2 neural layers; found {len(layers)}."
996:         )
997: 
998:     print()
999:     print(
1000:         "NETWORK ARCHITECTURE:"
1001:     )
1002: 
1003:     for i, layer in enumerate(
1004:         layers,
1005:         start=1,
1006:     ):
1007: 
1008:         print(
1009:             f"  Layer {i}: "
1010:             f"{len(layer['neurons'])} neurons "
1011:             f"activation={layer['activation']}"
1012:         )
1013: 
1014:     if (
1015:         len(layers[0]["neurons"]) != 7
1016:         or len(layers[1]["neurons"]) != 2
1017:     ):
1018: 
1019:         raise RuntimeError(
1020:             "Unexpected neural-network architecture."
1021:         )
1022: 
1023:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1024:     # Confirm output neuron IDs.
1025:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1026: 
1027:     output_ids = [
1028:         neuron["id"]
1029:         for neuron in layers[1]["neurons"]
1030:     ]
1031: 
1032:     print()
1033:     print(
1034:         "OUTPUT NEURONS:"
1035:     )
1036: 
1037:     for neuron_id in output_ids:
1038: 
1039:         print(
1040:             f"  {neuron_id}"
1041:         )
1042: 
1043:     # From the audited PMML:
1044:     #
1045:     #   21 = Ovarian Cancer
1046:     #   22 = Controls or Borderline
1047: 
1048:     if set(output_ids) != {"21", "22"}:
1049: 
1050:         raise RuntimeError(
1051:             "Expected output neurons 21 and 22; "
1052:             f"found {output_ids}."
1053:         )
1054: 
1055:     pmml = {
1056:         "model_name": model_name,
1057:         "function_name": function_name,
1058:         "inputs": pmml_inputs,
1059:         "layers": layers,
1060:         "cancer_output_neuron": "21",
1061:         "noncancer_output_neuron": "22",
1062:     }
1063: 
1064:     return pmml
1065: 
1066: 
1067: # =====================================================================
1068: # PMML FORWARD PASS
1069: # =====================================================================
1070: 
1071: def forward_pass(
1072:     X,
1073:     pmml,
1074: ):
1075: 
1076:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1077:     # Input normalization:
1078:     #
1079:     # The supplied PMML audit demonstrated that these particular
1080:     # NormContinuous transforms behave as:
1081:     #
1082:     #     normalized = x * scale + shift
1083:     #
1084:     # and the LinearNorm endpoints verify that relationship.
1085:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1086: 
1087:     normalized = np.zeros_like(
1088:         X,
1089:         dtype=np.float64,
1090:     )
1091: 
1092:     for j, spec in enumerate(
1093:         pmml["inputs"]
1094:     ):
1095: 
1096:         normalized[:, j] = (
1097:             X[:, j]
1098:             * spec["scale"]
1099:             + spec["shift"]
1100:         )
1101: 
1102:         # Verify supplied LinearNorm endpoints when present.
1103:         if len(spec["linear_norms"]) >= 2:
1104: 
1105:             orig_a, norm_a = (
1106:                 spec["linear_norms"][0]
1107:             )
1108: 
1109:             orig_b, norm_b = (
1110:                 spec["linear_norms"][1]
1111:             )
1112: 
1113:             calculated_a = (
1114:                 orig_a * spec["scale"]
1115:                 + spec["shift"]
1116:             )
1117: 
1118:             calculated_b = (
1119:                 orig_b * spec["scale"]
1120:                 + spec["shift"]
1121:             )
1122: 
1123:             if not math.isclose(
1124:                 calculated_a,
1125:                 norm_a,
1126:                 rel_tol=1e-7,
1127:                 abs_tol=1e-7,
1128:             ):
1129: 
1130:                 raise RuntimeError(
1131:                     f"PMML normalization check failed "
1132:                     f"for {spec['field']} at lower endpoint."
1133:                 )
1134: 
1135:             if not math.isclose(
1136:                 calculated_b,
1137:                 norm_b,
1138:                 rel_tol=1e-7,
1139:                 abs_tol=1e-7,
1140:             ):
1141: 
1142:                 raise RuntimeError(
1143:                     f"PMML normalization check failed "
1144:                     f"for {spec['field']} at upper endpoint."
1145:                 )
1146: 
1147:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1148:     # Hidden layer
1149:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1150: 
1151:     hidden_layer = pmml["layers"][0]
1152: 
1153:     if hidden_layer["activation"] != "tanh":
1154: 
1155:         raise RuntimeError(
1156:             "Historical hidden activation is not tanh."
1157:         )
1158: 
1159:     hidden = np.zeros(
1160:         (
1161:             X.shape[0],
1162:             len(hidden_layer["neurons"]),
1163:         ),
1164:         dtype=np.float64,
1165:     )
1166: 
1167:     input_names = [
1168:         str(i)
1169:         for i in range(
1170:             X.shape[1]
1171:         )
1172:     ]
1173: 
1174:     for j, neuron in enumerate(
1175:         hidden_layer["neurons"]
1176:     ):
1177: 
1178:         z = np.full(
1179:             X.shape[0],
1180:             neuron["bias"],
1181:             dtype=np.float64,
1182:         )
1183: 
1184:         for source, weight in (
1185:             neuron["connections"].items()
1186:         ):
1187: 
1188:             source_index = int(source)
1189: 
1190:             z += (
1191:                 normalized[:, source_index]
1192:                 * weight
1193:             )
1194: 
1195:         hidden[:, j] = np.tanh(z)
1196: 
1197:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1198:     # Output layer
1199:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
1200: 
1201:     output_layer = pmml["layers"][1]
1202: 
1203:     if output_layer["activation"] != "tanh":
1204: 
1205:         raise RuntimeError(
1206:             "Historical output activation is not tanh."
1207:         )
1208: 
1209:     outputs = np.zeros(
1210:         (
1211:             X.shape[0],
1212:             len(output_layer["neurons"]),
1213:         ),
1214:         dtype=np.float64,
1215:     )
1216: 
1217:     hidden_index_by_id = {
1218:         neuron["id"]: i
1219:         for i, neuron in enumerate(
1220:             hidden_layer["neurons"]
1221:         )
1222:     }
1223: 
1224:     for j, neuron in enumerate(
1225:         output_layer["neurons"]
1226:     ):
1227: 
1228:         z = np.full(
1229:             X.shape[0],
1230:             neuron["bias"],
1231:             dtype=np.float64,
1232:         )
1233: 
1234:         for source, weight in (
1235:             neuron["connections"].items()
1236:         ):
1237: 
1238:             if source not in hidden_index_by_id:
1239: 
1240:                 raise RuntimeError(
1241:                     "Output neuron references unknown "
1242:                     f"hidden neuron {source}."
1243:                 )
1244: 
1245:             source_index = (
1246:                 hidden_index_by_id[source]
1247:             )
1248: 
1249:             z += (
1250:                 hidden[:, source_index]
1251:                 * weight
1252:             )
1253: 
1254:         outputs[:, j] = np.tanh(z)
1255: 
1256:     output_index = {
1257:         neuron["id"]: i
1258:         for i, neuron in enumerate(
1259:             output_layer["neurons"]
1260:         )
1261:     }
1262: 
1263:     cancer_score = outputs[
1264:         :,
1265:         output_index[
1266:             pmml["cancer_output_neuron"]
1267:         ],
1268:     ]
1269: 
1270:     noncancer_score = outputs[
1271:         :,
1272:         output_index[
1273:             pmml["noncancer_output_neuron"]
1274:         ],
1275:     ]
1276: 
1277:     predicted_cancer = (
1278:         cancer_score > noncancer_score
1279:     ).astype(int)
1280: 
1281:     return (
1282:         normalized,
1283:         hidden,
1284:         outputs,
1285:         cancer_score,
1286:         noncancer_score,
1287:         predicted_cancer,
1288:     )
1289: 
1290: 
1291: # =====================================================================
1292: # METRICS
1293: # =====================================================================
1294: 
1295: def binary_metrics(
1296:     y_true,
1297:     y_pred,
1298:     score,
1299: ):
1300: 
1301:     y_true = np.asarray(
1302:         y_true,
1303:         dtype=int,
1304:     )
1305: 
1306:     y_pred = np.asarray(
1307:         y_pred,
1308:         dtype=int,
1309:     )
1310: 
1311:     score = np.asarray(
1312:         score,
1313:         dtype=float,
1314:     )
1315: 
1316:     tp = int(
1317:         np.sum(
1318:             (y_true == 1)
1319:             & (y_pred == 1)
1320:         )
1321:     )
1322: 
1323:     tn = int(
1324:         np.sum(
1325:             (y_true == 0)
1326:             & (y_pred == 0)
1327:         )
1328:     )
1329: 
1330:     fp = int(
1331:         np.sum(
1332:             (y_true == 0)
1333:             & (y_pred == 1)
1334:         )
1335:     )
1336: 
1337:     fn = int(
1338:         np.sum(
1339:             (y_true == 1)
1340:             & (y_pred == 0)
1341:         )
1342:     )
1343: 
1344:     sensitivity = (
1345:         tp / (tp + fn)
1346:         if (tp + fn) > 0
1347:         else float("nan")
1348:     )
1349: 
1350:     specificity = (
1351:         tn / (tn + fp)
1352:         if (tn + fp) > 0
1353:         else float("nan")
1354:     )
1355: 
1356:     accuracy = (
1357:         (tp + tn)
1358:         / max(
1359:             1,
1360:             len(y_true),
1361:         )
1362:     )
1363: 
1364:     auc = float("nan")
1365: 
1366:     try:
1367: 
1368:         from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
1369: 
1370:         if len(np.unique(y_true)) == 2:
1371: 
1372:             auc = float(
1373:                 roc_auc_score(
1374:                     y_true,
1375:                     score,
1376:                 )
1377:             )
1378: 
1379:     except Exception:
1380: 
1381:         pass
1382: 
1383:     return {
1384:         "auc": auc,
1385:         "accuracy": float(accuracy),
1386:         "sensitivity": float(sensitivity),
1387:         "specificity": float(specificity),
1388:         "tp": tp,
1389:         "tn": tn,
1390:         "fp": fp,
1391:         "fn": fn,
1392:     }
1393: 
1394: 
1395: # =====================================================================
1396: # MAIN
1397: # =====================================================================
1398:

### scripts\reproduce_original_pmml.py
1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: 
3: """
4: Reproduce the original eLife GSE94533 14-miRNA neural network.
5: 
6: IMPORTANT
7: ---------
8: This script DOES NOT train anything.
9: 
10: It implements the already-published PMML model directly from:
11: 
12:     original_pmml_deep_audit.json
13:     +
14:     gse94533_14mirna_benchmark.csv.gz
15: 
16: The model is:
17: 
18:     14 inputs
19:         ->
20:     7 tanh hidden neurons
21:         ->
22:     2 tanh output neurons
23: 
24: Input preprocessing is taken from the PMML:
25: 
26:     x_normalized = x * scale + shift
27: 
28: The PMML's two output neurons are:
29: 
30:     neuron 21 = Ovarian Cancer
31:     neuron 22 = Controls or Borderline
32: 
33: For classification, PMML uses the output neuron with the largest
34: activation to determine the predicted class.
35: 
36: For evaluation we additionally retain:
37: 
38:     cancer_score = activation(neuron 21)
39: 
40: This is a continuous model score.
41: 
42: We deliberately DO NOT call:
43: 
44:     (score + 1) / 2
45: 
46: or a softmax transformation an "original probability", because
47: the supplied PMML does not specify such a transformation for the
48: two tanh output neurons.
49: 
50: This is a research reproduction only. It is not a clinical
51: diagnostic system.
52: """
53: 
54: from __future__ import annotations
55: 
56: import json
57: import math
58: from pathlib import Path
59: 
60: import numpy as np
61: import pandas as pd
62: 
63: 
64: # ================================================================
65: # PATHS
66: # ================================================================
67: 
68: ROOT = Path.home() / "ovarian-ai"
69: 
70: DATASET_PATH = (
71:     ROOT
72:     / "data"
73:     / "processed"
74:     / "gse94533_14mirna_benchmark.csv.gz"
75: )
76: 
77: AUDIT_PATH = (
78:     ROOT
79:     / "reports"
80:     / "tables"
81:     / "original_pmml_deep_audit.json"
82: )
83: 
84: OUTPUT_DIR = (
85:     ROOT
86:     / "reports"
87:     / "tables"
88: )
89: 
90: PREDICTIONS_PATH = (
91:     OUTPUT_DIR
92:     / "original_pmml_predictions.csv"
93: )
94: 
95: RESULTS_PATH = (
96:     OUTPUT_DIR
97:     / "original_pmml_reproduction_results.json"
98: )
99: 
100: TRACE_PATH = (
101:     OUTPUT_DIR
102:     / "original_pmml_forward_pass_trace.csv"
103: )
104: 
105: 
106: # ================================================================
107: # EXACT HISTORICAL INPUT ORDER
108: # ================================================================
109: 
110: FEATURES = [
111:     "hsa-miR-23b-3p",
112:     "hsa-miR-29a-3p",
113:     "hsa-miR-32-5p",
114:     "hsa-miR-92a-3p",
115:     "hsa-miR-150-5p",
116:     "hsa-miR-200a-3p",
117:     "hsa-miR-200c-3p",
118:     "hsa-miR-203a",
119:     "hsa-miR-320c",
120:     "hsa-miR-320d",
121:     "hsa-miR-335-5p",
122:     "hsa-miR-450b-5p",
123:     "hsa-miR-1246",
124:     "hsa-miR-1307-5p",
125: ]
126: 
127: 
128: # ================================================================
129: # EXPECTED NETWORK STRUCTURE
130: # ================================================================
131: 
132: HIDDEN_IDS = [
133:     "14",
134:     "15",
135:     "16",
136:     "17",
137:     "18",
138:     "19",
139:     "20",
140: ]
141: 
142: OUTPUT_IDS = [
143:     "21",
144:     "22",
145: ]
146: 
147: 
148: # ================================================================
149: # ACTIVATION FUNCTIONS
150: # ================================================================
151: 
152: def tanh(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
153:     return np.tanh(x)
154: 
155: 
156: # ================================================================
157: # LOAD DATA
158: # ================================================================
159: 
160: def load_dataset() -> pd.DataFrame:
161: 
162:     if not DATASET_PATH.exists():
163: 
164:         raise RuntimeError(
165:             f"Dataset not found:\n{DATASET_PATH}"
166:         )
167: 
168:     df = pd.read_csv(
169:         DATASET_PATH
170:     )
171: 
172:     required = [
173:         "sample_id",
174:         "diagnosis",
175:         "binary_label",
176:     ] + FEATURES
177: 
178:     missing = [
179:         col
180:         for col in required
181:         if col not in df.columns
182:     ]
183: 
184:     if missing:
185: 
186:         raise RuntimeError(
187:             "Dataset missing required columns:\n"
188:             + "\n".join(
189:                 f"  {x}"
190:                 for x in missing
191:             )
192:         )
193: 
194:     return df
195: 
196: 
197: def load_audit():
198: 
199:     if not AUDIT_PATH.exists():
200: 
201:         raise RuntimeError(
202:             f"PMML audit not found:\n{AUDIT_PATH}"
203:         )
204: 
205:     return json.loads(
206:         AUDIT_PATH.read_text()
207:     )
208: 
209: 
210: # ================================================================
211: # EXTRACT PMML NORMALIZATION
212: # ================================================================
213: 
214: def extract_normalization(audit):
215: 
216:     """
217:     Extract the PMML normalization parameters.
218: 
219:     For STATISTICA-style PMML seen here:
220: 
221:         normalized = raw * scale + shift
222: 
223:     The LinearNorm endpoints independently confirm the same mapping.
224:     """
225: 
226:     neural_inputs = (
227:         audit[
228:             "neural_network"
229:         ][
230:             "neural_inputs"
231:         ]
232:     )
233: 
234:     normalization = {}
235: 
236:     for feature, neural_input in zip(
237:         FEATURES,
238:         neural_inputs,
239:     ):
240: 
241:         expressions = (
242:             neural_input.get(
243:                 "expressions",
244:                 []
245:             )
246:         )
247: 
248:         if len(expressions) != 1:
249: 
250:             raise RuntimeError(
251:                 f"Expected one expression for {feature}, "
252:                 f"found {len(expressions)}."
253:             )
254: 
255:         expression = expressions[0]
256: 
257:         if expression.get(
258:             "type"
259:         ) != "DerivedField":
260: 
261:             raise RuntimeError(
262:                 f"{feature}: expected DerivedField."
263:             )
264: 
265:         children = expression.get(
266:             "children",
267:             []
268:         )
269: 
270:         if len(children) != 1:
271: 
272:             raise RuntimeError(
273:                 f"{feature}: expected one DerivedField child."
274:             )
275: 
276:         norm = children[0]
277: 
278:         if norm.get(
279:             "type"
280:         ) != "NormContinuous":
281: 
282:             raise RuntimeError(
283:                 f"{feature}: expected NormContinuous."
284:             )
285: 
286:         attrs = norm.get(
287:             "attributes",
288:             {}
289:         )
290: 
291:         field = attrs.get(
292:             "field"
293:         )
294: 
295:         if field != feature:
296: 
297:             raise RuntimeError(
298:                 f"Feature mismatch: "
299:                 f"expected {feature}, "
300:                 f"PMML says {field}."
301:             )
302: 
303:         shift = float(
304:             attrs["shift"]
305:         )
306: 
307:         scale = float(
308:             attrs["scale"]
309:         )
310: 
311:         linear_norms = [
312:             child
313:             for child in norm.get(
314:                 "children",
315:                 []
316:             )
317:             if child.get(
318:                 "type"
319:             ) == "LinearNorm"
320:         ]
321: 
322:         if len(linear_norms) != 2:
323: 
324:             raise RuntimeError(
325:                 f"{feature}: expected exactly two LinearNorm elements."
326:             )
327: 
328:         orig0 = float(
329:             linear_norms[0][
330:                 "attributes"
331:             ][
332:                 "orig"
333:             ]
334:         )
335: 
336:         norm0 = float(
337:             linear_norms[0][
338:                 "attributes"
339:             ][
340:                 "norm"
341:             ]
342:         )
343: 
344:         orig1 = float(
345:             linear_norms[1][
346:                 "attributes"
347:             ][
348:                 "orig"
349:             ]
350:         )
351: 
352:         norm1 = float(
353:             linear_norms[1][
354:                 "attributes"
355:             ][
356:                 "norm"
357:             ]
358:         )
359: 
360:         # --------------------------------------------------------
361:         # Independent verification:
362:         #
363:         # y = (x - orig0)/(orig1 - orig0)
364:         #
365:         # should equal:
366:         #
367:         # y = x*scale + shift
368:         # --------------------------------------------------------
369: 
370:         expected_scale = (
371:             norm1 - norm0
372:         ) / (
373:             orig1 - orig0
374:         )
375: 
376:         expected_shift = (
377:             norm0
378:             - expected_scale * orig0
379:         )
380: 
381:         if not math.isclose(
382:             scale,
383:             expected_scale,
384:             rel_tol=1e-8,
385:             abs_tol=1e-10,
386:         ):
387: 
388:             raise RuntimeError(
389:                 f"{feature}: PMML scale does not agree with LinearNorm."
390:             )
391: 
392:         if not math.isclose(
393:             shift,
394:             expected_shift,
395:             rel_tol=1e-8,
396:             abs_tol=1e-10,
397:         ):
398: 
399:             raise RuntimeError(
400:                 f"{feature}: PMML shift does not agree with LinearNorm."
401:             )
402: 
403:         normalization[
404:             feature
405:         ] = {
406:             "shift": shift,
407:             "scale": scale,
408:             "orig_min": orig0,
409:             "orig_max": orig1,
410:             "norm_min": norm0,
411:             "norm_max": norm1,
412:         }
413: 
414:     return normalization
415: 
416: 
417: # ================================================================
418: # EXTRACT NEURAL NETWORK
419: # ================================================================
420: 
421: def extract_network(audit):
422: 
423:     nn = audit[
424:         "neural_network"
425:     ]
426: 
427:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
428:     # Check architecture.
429:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
430: 
431:     layers = nn[
432:         "neural_layers"
433:     ]
434: 
435:     if len(layers) != 2:
436: 
437:         raise RuntimeError(
438:             f"Expected 2 layers, found {len(layers)}."
439:         )
440: 
441:     hidden_layer = layers[0]
442:     output_layer = layers[1]
443: 
444:     if (
445:         hidden_layer[
446:             "activationFunction"
447:         ]
448:         != "tanh"
449:     ):
450: 
451:         raise RuntimeError(
452:             "Historical hidden layer is not tanh."
453:         )
454: 
455:     if (
456:         output_layer[
457:             "activationFunction"
458:         ]
459:         != "tanh"
460:     ):
461: 
462:         raise RuntimeError(
463:             "Historical output layer is not tanh."
464:         )
465: 
466:     if (
467:         hidden_layer[
468:             "numberOfNeurons"
469:         ]
470:         != 7
471:     ):
472: 
473:         raise RuntimeError(
474:             "Historical hidden layer does not contain 7 neurons."
475:         )
476: 
477:     if (
478:         output_layer[
479:             "numberOfNeurons"
480:         ]
481:         != 2
482:     ):
483: 
484:         raise RuntimeError(
485:             "Historical output layer does not contain 2 neurons."
486:         )
487: 
488:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
489:     # Convert neurons into numerical parameter matrices.
490:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
491: 
492:     hidden_weights = np.zeros(
493:         (
494:             7,
495:             14,
496:         ),
497:         dtype=float,
498:     )
499: 
500:     hidden_bias = np.zeros(
501:         7,
502:         dtype=float,
503:     )
504: 
505:     for i, neuron in enumerate(
506:         hidden_layer[
507:             "neurons"
508:         ]
509:     ):
510: 
511:         expected_id = HIDDEN_IDS[i]
512: 
513:         if neuron[
514:             "id"
515:         ] != expected_id:
516: 
517:             raise RuntimeError(
518:                 f"Unexpected hidden neuron order: "
519:                 f"expected {expected_id}, "
520:                 f"found {neuron['id']}."
521:             )
522: 
523:         hidden_bias[i] = float(
524:             neuron[
525:                 "bias"
526:             ]
527:         )
528: 
529:         connections = neuron[
530:             "connections"
531:         ]
532: 
533:         if len(connections) != 14:
534: 
535:             raise RuntimeError(
536:                 f"Neuron {expected_id} has "
537:                 f"{len(connections)} inputs; expected 14."
538:             )
539: 
540:         for connection in connections:
541: 
542:             source = str(
543:                 connection[
544:                     "from"
545:                 ]
546:             )
547: 
548:             source_index = int(
549:                 source
550:             )
551: 
552:             if not (
553:                 0
554:                 <= source_index
555:                 < 14
556:             ):
557: 
558:                 raise RuntimeError(
559:                     f"Invalid hidden-layer input index: {source}"
560:                 )
561: 
562:             hidden_weights[
563:                 i,
564:                 source_index,
565:             ] = float(
566:                 connection[
567:                     "weight"
568:                 ]
569:             )
570: 
571:     output_weights = np.zeros(
572:         (
573:             2,
574:             7,
575:         ),
576:         dtype=float,
577:     )
578: 
579:     output_bias = np.zeros(
580:         2,
581:         dtype=float,
582:     )
583: 
584:     for i, neuron in enumerate(
585:         output_layer[
586:             "neurons"
587:         ]
588:     ):
589: 
590:         expected_id = OUTPUT_IDS[i]
591: 
592:         if neuron[
593:             "id"
594:         ] != expected_id:
595: 
596:             raise RuntimeError(
597:                 f"Unexpected output neuron order: "
598:                 f"expected {expected_id}, "
599:                 f"found {neuron['id']}."
600:             )
601: 
602:         output_bias[i] = float(
603:             neuron[
604:                 "bias"
605:             ]
606:         )
607: 
608:         connections = neuron[
609:             "connections"
610:         ]
611: 
612:         if len(connections) != 7:
613: 
614:             raise RuntimeError(
615:                 f"Neuron {expected_id} has "
616:                 f"{len(connections)} hidden inputs; expected 7."
617:             )
618: 
619:         for connection in connections:
620: 
621:             source = str(
622:                 connection[
623:                     "from"
624:                 ]
625:             )
626: 
627:             if source not in HIDDEN_IDS:
628: 
629:                 raise RuntimeError(
630:                     f"Invalid output-layer source neuron: {source}"
631:                 )
632: 
633:             source_index = HIDDEN_IDS.index(
634:                 source
635:             )
636: 
637:             output_weights[
638:                 i,
639:                 source_index,
640:             ] = float(
641:                 connection[
642:                     "weight"
643:                 ]
644:             )
645: 
646:     return {
647:         "hidden_weights": hidden_weights,
648:         "hidden_bias": hidden_bias,
649:         "output_weights": output_weights,
650:         "output_bias": output_bias,
651:     }
652: 
653: 
654: # ================================================================
655: # FORWARD PASS
656: # ================================================================
657: 
658: def forward_pass(
659:     df: pd.DataFrame,
660:     normalization,
661:     network,
662: ):
663: 
664:     raw = df[
665:         FEATURES
666:     ].to_numpy(
667:         dtype=float
668:     )
669: 
670:     if not np.isfinite(
671:         raw
672:     ).all():
673: 
674:         raise RuntimeError(
675:             "Raw 14-miRNA data contain non-finite values."
676:         )
677: 
678:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
679:     # PMML input normalization.
680:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
681: 
682:     normalized = np.zeros_like(
683:         raw,
684:         dtype=float,
685:     )
686: 
687:     for j, feature in enumerate(
688:         FEATURES
689:     ):
690: 
691:         shift = normalization[
692:             feature
693:         ][
694:             "shift"
695:         ]
696: 
697:         scale = normalization[
698:             feature
699:         ][
700:             "scale"
701:         ]
702: 
703:         normalized[
704:             :,
705:             j
706:         ] = (
707:             raw[
708:                 :,
709:                 j
710:             ]
711:             * scale
712:             + shift
713:         )
714: 
715:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
716:     # Hidden layer.
717:     #
718:     # z = XW^T + bias
719:     # h = tanh(z)
720:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
721: 
722:     hidden_linear = (
723:         normalized
724:         @ network[
725:             "hidden_weights"
726:         ].T
727:         + network[
728:             "hidden_bias"
729:         ]
730:     )
731: 
732:     hidden_activation = tanh(
733:         hidden_linear
734:     )
735: 
736:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
737:     # Output layer.
738:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
739: 
740:     output_linear = (
741:         hidden_activation
742:         @ network[
743:             "output_weights"
744:         ].T
745:         + network[
746:             "output_bias"
747:         ]
748:     )
749: 
750:     output_activation = tanh(
751:         output_linear
752:     )
753: 
754:     return {
755:         "raw": raw,
756:         "normalized": normalized,
757:         "hidden_linear": hidden_linear,
758:         "hidden_activation": hidden_activation,
759:         "output_linear": output_linear,
760:         "output_activation": output_activation,
761:     }
762: 
763: 
764: # ================================================================
765: # METRICS
766: # ================================================================
767: 
768: def compute_confusion(
769:     y_true,
770:     y_pred,
771: ):
772: 
773:     y_true = np.asarray(
774:         y_true,
775:         dtype=int,
776:     )
777: 
778:     y_pred = np.asarray(
779:         y_pred,
780:         dtype=int,
781:     )
782: 
783:     tp = int(
784:         (
785:             (y_true == 1)
786:             & (y_pred == 1)
787:         ).sum()
788:     )
789: 
790:     tn = int(
791:         (
792:             (y_true == 0)
793:             & (y_pred == 0)
794:         ).sum()
795:     )
796: 
797:     fp = int(
798:         (
799:             (y_true == 0)
800:             & (y_pred == 1)
801:         ).sum()
802:     )
803: 
804:     fn = int(
805:         (
806:             (y_true == 1)
807:             & (y_pred == 0)
808:         ).sum()
809:     )
810: 
811:     sensitivity = (
812:         tp / (tp + fn)
813:         if tp + fn
814:         else None
815:     )
816: 
817:     specificity = (
818:         tn / (tn + fp)
819:         if tn + fp
820:         else None
821:     )
822: 
823:     accuracy = (
824:         (tp + tn)
825:         / len(y_true)
826:     )
827: 
828:     return {
829:         "tp": tp,
830:         "tn": tn,
831:         "fp": fp,
832:         "fn": fn,
833:         "sensitivity": sensitivity,
834:         "specificity": specificity,
835:         "accuracy": accuracy,
836:     }
837: 
838: 
839: def compute_auc(
840:     y_true,
841:     score,
842: ):
843: 
844:     """
845:     Calculate ROC AUC without requiring sklearn.
846: 
847:     Uses the rank/Mann-Whitney formulation.
848: 
849:     AUC = probability that a randomly chosen positive receives
850:     a higher score than a randomly chosen negative, with ties
851:     receiving half credit.
852:     """
853: 
854:     y_true = np.asarray(
855:         y_true,
856:         dtype=int,
857:     )
858: 
859:     score = np.asarray(
860:         score,
861:         dtype=float,
862:     )
863: 
864:     positive = score[
865:         y_true == 1
866:     ]
867: 
868:     negative = score[
869:         y_true == 0
870:     ]
871: 
872:     if len(positive) == 0:
873:         return None
874: 
875:     if len(negative) == 0:
876:         return None
877: 
878:     wins = 0.0
879: 
880:     for p in positive:
881: 
882:         wins += (
883:             (p > negative)
884:         ).sum()
885: 
886:         wins += 0.5 * (
887:             (p == negative)
888:         ).sum()
889: 
890:     auc = (
891:         wins
892:         / (
893:             len(positive)
894:             * len(negative)
895:         )
896:     )
897: 
898:     return float(
899:         auc
900:     )
901:

948:         "Output activation: tanh"

979:     # Neuron 22 = Controls or Borderline
980:     #
981:     # Larger activation wins.
982:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
983:

985:         cancer_score
986:         > noncancer_score

988:         int
989:     )
990:

992:         "binary_label"
993:     ].to_numpy(
994:         dtype=int
995:     )

1002:         y_true,
1003:         predicted_class,

1005:

1007:         y_true,
1008:         cancer_score,
1009:     )
1010: 
1011:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
1012:     # Exact equality check.
1013:     #
1014:     # Because the output neurons in the original network are
1015:     # nearly opposite, this should behave as expected.

1017:

1019:         cancer_score
1020:         == noncancer_score
1021:     )

1028:         {
1029:             "sample_id": df[
1030:                 "sample_id"
1031:             ],
1032:             "diagnosis": df[
1033:                 "diagnosis"
1034:             ],
1035:             "true_binary_label": y_true,
1036:             "cancer_output_neuron_21": cancer_score,
1037:             "noncancer_output_neuron_22": noncancer_score,
1038:             "output_margin_21_minus_22": (
1039:                 cancer_score
1040:                 - noncancer_score
1041:             ),
1042:             "predicted_binary_label": predicted_class,
1043:             "predicted_class": np.where(
1044:                 predicted_class == 1,
1045:                 "Ovarian Cancer",
1046:                 "Controls or Borderline",
1047:             ),
1048:         }
1049:     )

1052:         PREDICTIONS_PATH,
1053:         index=False,
1054:     )

1066:                 "sample_id"
1067:             ],
1068:         }
1069:     )
1070: 
1071:     for j, feature in enumerate(
1072:         FEATURES
1073:     ):
1074: 
1075:         trace[
1076:             f"raw_{feature}"
1077:         ] = forward[
1078:             "raw"
1079:         ][
1080:             :,
1081:             j
1082:         ]
1083: 
1084:         trace[
1085:             f"normalized_{feature}"
1086:         ] = forward[
1087:             "normalized"
1088:         ][
1089:             :,
1090:             j
1091:         ]
1092: 
1093:     for i, neuron_id in enumerate(
1094:         HIDDEN_IDS
1095:     ):
1096: 
1097:         trace[
1098:             f"hidden_{neuron_id}_linear"
1099:         ] = forward[
1100:             "hidden_linear"
1101:         ][
1102:             :,
1103:             i
1104:         ]
1105:

1107:             f"hidden_{neuron_id}_activation"
1108:         ] = forward[
1109:             "hidden_activation"
1110:         ][
1111:             :,
1112:             i
1113:         ]

1116:         "output_21_linear"
1117:     ] = forward[
1118:         "output_linear"
1119:     ][
1120:         :,
1121:         0
1122:     ]
1123: 
1124:     trace[
1125:         "output_21_activation"
1126:     ] = cancer_score
1127:

1129:         "output_22_linear"

1131:         "output_linear"
1132:     ][

1157:

1159:             len(df)
1160:         ),
1161: 
1162:         "historical_model": {
1163:             "model_name": (
1164:                 "Dataset complete with classificat_MLP 14-7-2"
1165:             ),

1167:             "input_features": 14,

1173:             "noncancer_output_neuron": "22",

1178:             "source": str(

### scripts\reproduce_original_pmml_historical_data.py
1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: 
3: """
4: Reproduce the original eLife GSE94533 neural network using the
5: HISTORICAL DATA REPRESENTATION rather than our raw-TPM matrix.
6: 
7: Why this script exists
8: ----------------------
9: 
10: The previous reproduction produced:
11: 
12:     AUC = 0.451682
13:     sensitivity = 0
14:     specificity = 1
15: 
16: That strongly suggested that the neural network itself was being
17: fed the wrong representation of the data.
18: 
19: The PMML normalization anchors are in ranges such as:
20: 
21:     hsa-miR-23b-3p:
22:         0.1816 -> 1.8782
23: 
24: and the eLife supplementary workbook identifies Supplemental Dataset 2
25: as:
26: 
27:     "Batch adjusted, log10-transformed miRNA expression data"
28: 
29: Those ranges are consistent with the PMML inputs.
30: 
31: Therefore the historical network should be evaluated on Supplemental
32: Dataset 2 rather than the raw TPM matrix.
33: 
34: This script:
35: 
36:     Supplemental Dataset 2
37:             |
38:             v
39:     179 historical sample positions
40:             |
41:             v
42:     map positions to actual GSE94533 sample IDs
43:             |
44:             v
45:     exact 14 PMML features
46:             |
47:             v
48:     PMML normalization
49:             |
50:             v
51:     14 -> 7 tanh -> 2 tanh
52:             |
53:             v
54:     historical predictions
55: 
56: NO MODEL TRAINING IS PERFORMED.
57: """

146: def normalize_id(value):
147: 
148:     if pd.isna(value):
149:         return ""
150: 
151:     s = str(value).strip().lower()
152: 
153:     # Numeric Excel identifiers such as 50217.0
154:     if s.endswith(".0"):
155:         try:
156:             s = str(int(float(s)))
157:         except Exception:
158:             pass
159: 
160:     # E-1001 -> e1001
161:     s = (
162:         s
163:         .replace("-", "")
164:         .replace("_", "")
165:         .replace(" ", "")
166:     )
167: 
168:     return s
169:

301: def load_supplemental_dataset_2():
302: 
303:     print()
304:     print("=" * 100)
305:     print("READING SUPPLEMENTAL DATASET 2")
306:     print("=" * 100)
307: 
308:     if not SUPPLEMENTARY_XLSX.exists():
309: 
310:         raise RuntimeError(
311:             f"Supplementary workbook not found:\n"
312:             f"{SUPPLEMENTARY_XLSX}"
313:         )
314:

316:         SUPPLEMENTARY_XLSX,
317:         sheet_name="Supplemental Dataset 2",
318:         header=None,
319:         engine="openpyxl",
320:     )
321: 
322:     print()
323:     print(
324:         f"Raw shape: {raw.shape}"
325:     )
326: 
327:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
328:     # IMPORTANT
329:     #
330:     # Supplemental Dataset 2 does NOT necessarily use:
331:     #
332:     #     1, 2, 3, ..., 179
333:     #
334:     # as its column headers.
335:     #
336:     # Depending on how Excel/pandas interprets the supplementary
337:     # workbook, the sample header row can contain the REAL GSE IDs:
338:     #
339:     #     e1036
340:     #     e1048
341:     #     ...
342:     #     50217
343:     #     80675
344:     #
345:     # Therefore we detect the sample-ID row rather than assuming
346:     # numeric sample positions.
347:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
348: 
349:     def local_normalize_id(value):
350: 
351:         if pd.isna(value):
352:             return ""
353: 
354:         s = str(value).strip().lower()
355: 
356:         # Handle Excel numeric values such as 50217.0.
357:         if s.endswith(".0"):
358: 
359:             try:
360:                 s = str(int(float(s)))
361:             except Exception:
362:                 pass
363: 
364:         s = (
365:             s
366:             .replace("-", "")
367:             .replace("_", "")
368:             .replace(" ", "")
369:         )
370: 
371:         return s
372: 
373:     def looks_like_sample_id(value):
374: 
375:         s = local_normalize_id(value)
376: 
377:         if not s:
378:             return False
379: 
380:         # e1036-style Cohort 1 IDs.
381:         if s.startswith("e") and s[1:].isdigit():
382:             return True
383: 
384:         # Numeric Cohort 2 IDs.
385:         if s.isdigit():
386:             return True
387: 
388:         return False
389: 
390:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
391:     # Detect the row containing the 179 actual sample IDs.
392:     #
393:     # We search the first several rows and count how many cells after
394:     # column zero look like real sample identifiers.
395:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
396: 
397:     sample_header_candidates = []
398: 
399:     search_rows = min(
400:         20,
401:         len(raw),
402:     )
403: 
404:     for row_idx in range(
405:         search_rows
406:     ):
407: 
408:         values = raw.iloc[
409:             row_idx,
410:             1:
411:         ].tolist()
412: 
413:         ids_here = [
414:             local_normalize_id(x)
415:             for x in values
416:             if looks_like_sample_id(x)
417:         ]
418: 
419:         unique_ids_here = set(
420:             ids_here
421:         )
422: 
423:         sample_header_candidates.append(
424:             (
425:                 row_idx,
426:                 len(ids_here),
427:                 len(unique_ids_here),
428:                 ids_here,
429:             )
430:         )
431: 
432:     # Prefer a row with 179 distinct sample IDs.
433:     exact_candidates = [
434:         x
435:         for x in sample_header_candidates
436:         if x[2] == 179
437:     ]
438: 
439:     if exact_candidates:
440: 
441:         sample_header_row = exact_candidates[0][0]
442: 
443:     else:
444: 
445:         # Otherwise choose the row with the greatest number of
446:         # unique sample-like identifiers.
447:         ranked = sorted(
448:             sample_header_candidates,
449:             key=lambda x: (
450:                 x[2],
451:                 x[1],
452:             ),
453:             reverse=True,
454:         )
455: 
456:         if not ranked or ranked[0][2] < 100:
457: 
458:             print()
459:             print(
460:                 "Could not identify the historical sample-ID row."
461:             )
462: 
463:             print()
464:             print(
465:                 "Candidate rows:"
466:             )
467: 
468:             for row_idx, count, unique_count, ids_here in ranked:
469:                 print(
470:                     f"  row={row_idx:2d} "
471:                     f"sample_like={count:3d} "
472:                     f"unique={unique_count:3d} "
473:                     f"first_ids={ids_here[:10]}"
474:                 )
475: 
476:             raise RuntimeError(
477:                 "Could not safely identify the Supplemental Dataset 2 "
478:                 "sample-ID header row."
479:             )
480: 
481:         sample_header_row = ranked[0][0]
482: 
483:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
484:     # Recover the actual sample IDs in the order they occur in the
485:     # supplementary workbook.
486:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
487: 
488:     sample_ids = []
489: 
490:     sample_column_indices = []
491: 
492:     for col_idx in range(
493:         1,
494:         raw.shape[1],
495:     ):
496: 
497:         value = raw.iloc[
498:             sample_header_row,
499:             col_idx
500:         ]
501: 
502:         if looks_like_sample_id(value):
503: 
504:             normalized = local_normalize_id(
505:                 value
506:             )
507: 
508:             sample_ids.append(
509:                 normalized
510:             )
511: 
512:             sample_column_indices.append(
513:                 col_idx
514:             )
515: 
516:     print()
517:     print(
518:         f"Detected sample-ID header row: {sample_header_row}"
519:     )
520: 
521:     print(
522:         f"Detected sample columns: {len(sample_ids)}"
523:     )
524: 
525:     print()
526:     print(
527:         "First sample IDs:"
528:     )
529: 
530:     for sample_id in sample_ids[:15]:
531: 
532:         print(
533:             f"  {sample_id}"
534:         )
535: 
536:     print()
537:     print(
538:         "Last sample IDs:"
539:     )
540: 
541:     for sample_id in sample_ids[-15:]:
542: 
543:         print(
544:             f"  {sample_id}"
545:         )
546: 
547:     # ---------------------------------------------------------------
548:     # IMPORTANT HISTORICAL DATASET DETAIL
549:     #
550:     # Supplemental Dataset 2 uses POSITIONAL sample numbers:
551:     #
552:     #     1, 2, 3, ..., 179
553:     #
554:     # These are NOT the actual GSE94533 sample identifiers.
555:     #
556:     # The original supplementary Dataset 1 makes clear that the
557:     # historical 179-sample matrix consists of:
558:     #
559:     #     first 120 = Cohort 2 numeric sample IDs
560:     #     next 59   = Cohort 1 E-#### IDs

566:     #     Dataset-2 position
567:     #             |
568:     #             v
569:     #     recovered original sample order

573:     #

577:

579:         str(i)

581:             1,
582:             180,
583:         )
584:     ]

586:     if sample_ids == positional_ids:
587: 
588:         print()
589:         print(
590:             "Detected positional sample headers 1..179."
591:         )

599:

641:

670: 
671:         if len(recovered_order) != 179:
672:             raise RuntimeError(

674:                 f"{len(recovered_order)} samples; expected 179."
675:             )
676:

678:             normalize_id(x)
679:             for x in recovered_order
680:         ]
681: 
682:         # First 120 entries must correspond to Cohort 2.
683:         cohort2_ids = recovered_order[:120]
684: 
685:         # Final 59 entries in Dataset 2 are explicit Cohort 1 IDs.
686:         explicit_cohort1_ids = [
687:             normalize_id(x)
688:             for x in sample_ids[120:]
689:         ]
690: 
691:         # The recovered historical order also contains the expected
692:         # Cohort 1 sequence.
693:         expected_cohort1_ids = recovered_order[120:]
694: 
695:         if explicit_cohort1_ids != expected_cohort1_ids:
696: 
697:             print()

699:                 "ERROR: Dataset 2 Cohort 1 ordering does not "
700:                 "match the recovered historical order."

703:             print()
704:             print(

706:             )
707:

712:                 print(
713:                     f"  {position:3d} -> {value}"
714:                 )
715:

717:             print(

719:             )
720:

723:                 start=121,
724:             ):

727:                 )
728: 
729:             raise RuntimeError(
